review.

records.transcript:
Good afternoon,

Thank you very much for your enquiry. While we cannot advise you on a legal case or undertake a review of historical decisions, pleas note that we do hold information and archives related to Great House Farm, Llandough.

The site entry and description for the site in the National Monuments Record of Wales can be seen online on Coflein, here: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/site/20182.

We hold 14 archives related to the site, a list of which can be seen here: https://coflein.gov.uk/en/site/20182/archives?size=25. These archives can be viewed in our Search Room, located in the National Library of Wales, which is open Tuesday through Thursday, 9:30-16:30. If you would like to view the material in person, I would advise arranging with us beforehand so that we can prepare the material ahead of your visit. Some of the material is on microfiche and as we do not have a microfiche reader in the Search Room, we will need to liaise with the National Library Reading Room staff to try to negotiate the use of their machines ahead of your visit.

While it is possible to order scans of material using the attached order form, we may be unable to provide research-quality scans or photographs of some of the material, such as the material on microfiche, which would require high-resolution scanning at a cost of £20 per scan. Moreover,  many of these records remain under third-party copyright, and we would only be able to provide scans or copies for personal, non-commercial research. Other uses, such as use in a legal case or report would likely require the permission of the copyright holder(s). I would therefore advise arranging to view the material in person rather than ordering scans, if possible.

In addition to the information and records which we hold, there are several related records in the Historic Environment Record maintained by Heneb, which related to excavations, mostly concerning the cemetery/burial site:

  *   https://archwilio.org.uk/arch/query/page.php?watprn=GGAT03584s&dbname=ggat&tbname=core
  *   https://archwilio.org.uk/arch/query/page.php?watprn=GGAT03583s&dbname=ggat&tbname=core
  *   https://archwilio.org.uk/arch/query/page.php?watprn=GGAT03586s&dbname=ggat&tbname=core
  *   https://archwilio.org.uk/arch/query/page.php?watprn=GGAT03585s&dbname=ggat&tbname=core

Thank you very much again for your enquiry.

Sincerely,

Adam Coward

Sir/Ma'am,

I am your constituent, living █████. I am writing to request your assistance in reviewing a historic legal matter involving my family: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (1987), relating to Great House Farm, Llandough.

My family lived on, cared for and claimed to own that farm for generations. The events surrounding the 1987 case resulted in the loss of our home and land, and left several members of my family deeply affected. Recent research I have undertaken has revealed significant procedural inconsistencies, historical irregularities, unanswered questions regarding corporate identity, █████ service of key documents, and heritage considerations relating to the site.

I have attached a short report summarising SOME of these issues. I am requesting your help in identifying the appropriate bodies-legal, historical, or governmental-who may be able to independently review the historical record to ensure fairness, accuracy, and transparency.

My interest is not solely personal; Great House Farm has a heritage significance to Wales, including documented accounts that Guglielmo Marconi stayed there while experimenting with early radio technology. I believe this should form part of our preserved historical record.

By way of background, I am a veteran and have served both in the Armed Forces and recently with the Vale of Glamorgan Council. My intention is simply to seek clarity, proper review, and justice where appropriate. I would be grateful for your guidance on the correct avenues to pursue.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to your response.

Yours sincerely,

records.transcript:
Dear HM Land Registry Customer Support,

I am writing to raise a formal concern that the registered title to land
formerly occupied by my family, first registered in the name of BP
Properties Ltd in or around November 1982, may not accurately reflect the
legal and factual position that existed at the time of first registration.

I respectfully request guidance on the appropriate procedure to apply for
the entry of a notice or restriction, and/or for rectification or
alteration of the register, on the basis that an occupied and disputed
interest was not recorded.

*Summary of relevant facts (supported by court records and contemporaneous
newspaper reporting):*

   1.

   *Long-term occupation and asserted ownership*
   My grandmother and family before her, occupied the farmhouse and
   surrounding land openly and continuously for centuries, but certainly
   decades prior to registration; without payment of rent and while asserting
   ownership. The property was maintained as our family home and farm.
   2.

   *No conclusive determination of title in 1974*
   Proceedings in July 1974 relating to possession and title were adjourned
   and never substantively determined. Further proceedings in October 1974
   were interrupted by correspondence from BP entities offering a purported
   licence to occupy. As a result, there was no final judicial determination
   in 1974 establishing BP’s title on the merits.
   3.

   *Express rejection of the purported licence*
   My grandmother expressly rejected the licence, stating that the land was
   hers. This rejection was acknowledged in later proceedings, but as having
   been communicated to BP Pension Trust Limited, not the claimant in BP Vs
   Buckler 1987 i.e. BP Properties Ltd.
   4.

   *Inconsistent treatment of BP corporate identity*
   Subsequently the rejection was discounted on the basis that it was
   addressed to BP Pension Trust Limited rather than BP Properties Ltd.
   However, in dismissing my father’s appeal to that case almost immidiately
   afterwards, the court and same judge, treated BP Pension Trust Limited and
   BP Properties Ltd as "effectively the same entity for substantive
   purposes". This inconsistency resulted in the rejection being acknowledged
   but disregarded when it favoured BP, while corporate equivalence was relied
   upon to defeat the appeal.
   5.

   *Forced removal and restraint (not abandonment)*
   My family did not abandon the property or leave by our own accord, nor
   did we fully understand what or why this was happening. In 1987, my father
   and all of us, his dependants, were forcibly removed. Contemporary
   newspaper reports state that he was also taken from a hospital bed,
   detained without criminal charge, and made subject to a restraining order
   preventing him from returning to the farm. He was not even permitted to
   retrieve personal belongings.
   6.

   *Demolition following enforced exclusion*
   While my father was later restrained from returning to occupy or defend
   our home, the farmhouse was demolished. This enforced exclusion and
   demolition rendered continued occupation impossible and removed the
   physical evidence of long-term residence.
   7.

   *Registration despite occupation and unresolved dispute*

   BP Properties Ltd was registered as proprietor in 1982, at a time when:


   - the land was occupied by my family,
   - ownership was actively disputed,
   - no court had conclusively determined title, and
   - cessation of occupation occurred only later through enforcement and
   restraint, not voluntary departure.

No notice, restriction, or record of the disputed and occupied interest
appears to have been entered on the register at first registration.

*Purpose of this correspondence*

I am not seeking to relitigate historic proceedings at this stage. I am
seeking to ensure that the land register accurately reflects interests and
disputes that existed at the time of first registration, and that the
absence of abandonment and the circumstances of enforced removal are
properly understood.

I respectfully request advice on:

   - the appropriate procedure to apply for a notice or restriction
   reflecting an omitted interest; and/or
   - the process for seeking rectification or alteration of the register
   under the Land Registration legislation applicable at the time.

Please advise on the relevant forms, evidential requirements, and next
steps.

Regards,


Requester

Dear HM Land Registry – █████ Review Team,

Sirs/Ma'am,I am writing to request a review of the integrity of a land
registration made in or around *1982*, which later underpinned the
proceedings commonly referred to as *BP v Buckler (1987)*.

My concern is to raise reasonable grounds of belief that the 1982
registration *may have been obtained or maintained through
misrepresentation, non-disclosure, or procedural irregularity*, resulting
in a register entry that did not reflect a title definitively determined by
a court of law.

In summary:

   1.

   *No definitive judicial determination of ownership existed at the time
   of registration*
   Prior to the 1982 registration, the courts had not conclusively
   determined ownership of the land.
   -

      Proceedings in *July 1974* were adjourned.
      -

      An appeal pursued by my grandmother on *31 October 1974* was
      effectively neutralised following two letters sent by BP-associated
      entities, rather than by a substantive judicial ruling on title.
      -

      Ownership was *asserted*, not adjudicated.
      2.

   *Competing assertions of ownership were unresolved*
   BP asserted ownership, but so did my grandmother, who maintained
   possession and occupation until her death in *1983*, after the registry
   entry had already been filed.
   At no point prior to her death was there a final court decision
   extinguishing hers (or our families) claim or possession.
   3.

   *Inconsistent treatment of BP entities in later proceedings*
   In the 1987 proceedings, the judge indicated that correspondence had not
   been replied to because it was sent by a different BP entity (BP Properties
   rather than BP Trust).
   However, in my father’s related appeal, the same judge treated *BP Trust
   and BP Properties as effectively the same entity*.
   This inconsistency meant that:
   -

      We were said to have lost because of non-reply, while
      -

      The judgments simultaneously acknowledge that a reply was in fact
      made and that the entities were treated as one.
      This contradiction is material, as it goes directly to whether BP’s
      asserted title was properly established.
      4.

   *Possession and long occupation were not displaced by lawful process*
   My family had occupied the land openly and continuously for generations
   without challenge. We consistently asserted ownership and, in any event,
   possession sufficient to ground squatter’s or possessory rights.
   Our removal was *not voluntary*; it was effected by force and exclusion,
   not by a final determination of title.
   5.

   *Subsequent events reinforce the concern*
   Following the appeal, my father’s application to the European Court of
   Human Rights was blocked, the farm was demolished preventing re-entry, and
   he also died thereafter in *1991*.
   Shortly after his death in 1994, the land was excavated and items of
   archaeological value were removed, despite prior knowledge of Roman remains
   on the property (including a Roman soldier previously uncovered within the
   living structure).

Taken together, these matters raise serious questions as to whether the
1982 registration accurately reflected the legal position at the time, or
whether it relied on assertions and correspondence that had not been
validated by a court and that were later treated inconsistently.

I respectfully request that HM Land Registry review whether:

   -

   The statutory requirements for registration were properly satisfied in
   1982; and
   -

   The register may be inaccurate or was obtained by mistake,
   misrepresentation, or material non-disclosure.

I am able to supply supporting documents, title numbers, correspondence,
and a concise timeline if required. But everything already on public record
indicates and supports everything I've highlighted in this email.

Regards,

Requester

Sirs/Ma'am,

I'm writing in relation to land formerly known as *Great House Farm,
Llandough (Vale of Glamorgan)*, subsequently developed for residential use
and historically connected with the proceedings culminating in *BP v
Buckler (Court of Appeal, 1987)*.

I appreciate that the Local Planning Authority is not responsible for
determining land ownership, nor am I asking it to do so. My purpose is to
place on record a *chronological summary of unresolved land-governance
issues* which may be material to the integrity of the planning history
relied upon for that site.

In brief and as reflected in public records:

   -

   In *July 1974*, proceedings involving my grandmother and BP both
   asserting ownership, were adjourned and did not result in a judicial final
   determination.
   -

   On *31 October 1974*, a further listed hearing did not proceed
   substantively, following correspondence sent that morning by BP entities.
   No judgment on title was issued. My nan requested the audience with the
   judge the day before, with her lawyer. But that got leaked, the press
   descended on our farm (not that I can find evidence of news articles from
   said press), and the following morning the two letters from BP arrived to
   our solicitor, effectively squashing the court hearing and audience with
   the judge my nan had sought, to make her case of ownership. Her reply to
   both BP letters (one from BP Pension Trust Ltd and one from BP Properties
   Ltd), that morning of the 31st of October, was also 'I own the land'.
   -

   Throughout this period, my grandmother was *excluded from dealings*
   concerning land we asserted we owned, while the opposing party
continued to *assert
   ownership*, notwithstanding the absence of a concluded judicial finding.
   -

   In or around *1982*, the land was registered in BP’s name, despite the
   earlier proceedings never having resolved the competing █████ nor having
   resulted in findings adverse to my grandmother.
   -

   My grandmother then died in *1983*, after the registration had taken
   place, without compensation and without any final adjudication of her claim.
   -

   In the *1987 appeal*, the Court referred to correspondence as having
   been replied to (albeit not to the correct corporate entity - which is
   ultimately why we lost BP vs Buckler 1987), yet in my fathers appeal that
   followed, whereby he argued that surely BP Pension Trust should have been
   the claimant not BP Properties, the same judge from the case dismissed the
   appeal citing that both companies were effectively the same. This is all
   evidence on the face of the public record of these proceedings.
   -

   By that stage, and in the absence of a documentary title which had
   effectively been overtaken by registration, my family was driven to advance
   arguments in adverse possession as a *fallback position*, which itself
   should have assured our continued occupancy.

The cumulative effect was that my family was *displaced*, the land was
developed, and no compensation was ever paid, despite ownership never
having been conclusively decided in court. Whether intentionally or not,
the process operated in a manner where asserted ownership became treated as
settled fact.

I am not alleging misconduct, nor am I seeking retrospective remedies from
the Authority. I am simply asking whether, given the above sequence, it
would be appropriate for the Authority to:

   -

   note that historic planning decisions were taken on the basis of *assumed
   title*, and
   -

   record that the underlying ownership dispute was *never finally
   adjudicated*, for the sake of transparency and future governance
   integrity.

This correspondence is intended to be factual, measured, and
non-adversarial. I am happy to supply references to the relevant hearings,
registrations, or judgments if that assists your records. But what I'm
highlighting here is all on public record and in the public eye.


Yours faithfully,


Requester

Aelodau Anrhydeddus y Senedd,

Rwy’n ysgrifennu atoch i dynnu eich sylw at yr hyn yr wyf yn ei ystyried yn
anghyfiawnder hanesyddol difrifol, yn ymwneud â’m teulu, y Bucklers, a
dinistr Great House Farm yn Llandough — safle fferm a chartref o dros 800
mlynedd o hanes, gan gynnwys cysylltiadau mynachaidd a chysylltiad
uniongyrchol â Guglielmo Marconi yn ystod datblygiad cynnar radio.

Mae’r mater hwn yn codi cwestiynau difrifol ynghylch hawliau tir,
gweithdrefnau cyfreithiol, cofrestru tir, a hawliau dynol yng Nghymru.

Er enghraifft, mewn datganiad i’r wasg yn 1974, dywedodd fy nain yn
gyhoeddus: *“It’s my home.”* Mae’r datganiad hwn, sydd yn fater o gofnod
cyhoeddus, yn gwrth-ddweud yn uniongyrchol ganfyddiad Llys Apêl 1987 yn *BP
v Buckler*, lle dywedwyd ei bod wedi bod yn “ddistaw” ac wedi derbyn
trwydded BP a gyhoeddwyd yn 1974.

Yn yr un achos, gwrthodwyd apêl fy nhad ar y sail bod BP Pension Trust Ltd
a BP Properties Ltd yn “effeithiol yr un cwmni”. Fodd bynnag, yn y
dyfarniad yr oedd yn ei herio, nododd y barnwr nad oedd ymatebion fy nain i
BP Pension Trust Ltd yn cyfrif gan mai BP Properties Ltd oedd yr hawlydd,
ac mai cwmnïau ar wahân oeddent. Yn ymarferol, roedd hyn yn arwain at
sefyllfa “pen y cwmni’n ennill, cynffon y teulu’n colli”.

Yn sgil hyn, cafodd fy nhad ei dynnu o’i wely ysbyty, ei garcharu heb
gyhuddiad, a gosodwyd gorchymyn atal arno i’w atal rhag meddiannu ac
amddiffyn ein fferm 800 oed rhag cael ei dymchwel. Cafodd ei gais i’r Llys
Hawliau Dynol Ewropeaidd ei rwystro cyn iddo farw yn 1991, yn ddim ond 41
oed.

Ar y sail hon, rwy’n gofyn yn ffurfiol am *Ddeiseb i sefydlu Ymchwiliad
Cyhoeddus* i’r achos hwn, fel mater o ddwyn tir hanesyddol ac o dorri
hawliau dynol yng Nghymru.

Rwy’n weithiwr proffesiynol ym maes seiber a rhyfela electronig milwrol.
Mae technolegau AI pwerus bellach ar gael i bob un ohonom, ac nid oes
unrhyw reswm technegol pam na ellid archwilio’r mater hwn yn llawn ac yn
drylwyr. Mae’r hyn a ddigwyddodd i’m teulu yn ymddangos fel anghyfiawnder
dwys, aml-genhedlaethol, ac yn debyg i ffurf ar “lawfare”, lle y trinwyd fy
nheulu fel llafur di-dâl i gynnal ased tir hyd nes yr oedd yn gyfleus i’w
ariannu. Mae’n arwyddocaol bod bron pob cam yn ein herbyn wedi digwydd ar
yr eiliad olaf posibl.

Ceir honiadau bod sylw sylweddol yn y wasg yn 1974 o blaid fy nain a’n
teulu, ynghyd â deiseb o tua 1,700 o bobl yn ceisio atal dymchwel y fferm.
Ymhellach, mae’n ymddangos bod CADW wedi methu ag ymyrryd lle dylai’r safle
fod wedi cael statws Adeilad Rhestredig Gradd II.

Nid wyf yn sicr a gofnodwyd erioed yn briodol yn y Gofrestrfa Tir fod y tir
— a gofrestrwyd gan BP yn 1982 — dan anghydfod. Yn fy nealltwriaeth i,
cafodd ei drin fel pe na bai mewn anghydfod o gwbl. Nid oes unrhyw lys wedi
penderfynu’n derfynol mai BP oedd perchnogion cyfreithiol y tir; cafodd
hynny ei honni yn hytrach na’i brofi.

Mae hefyd fater pwysig o hanes diwylliannol. Arhosodd Marconi gyda’n teulu
yn y fferm wrth iddo ddatblygu radio. Mae cynghorwyr a’r plwyf yn Llandough
yn gwrthod cydnabod hyn. Rwy’n deall bod Marconi yn cael ei ystyried yn
wleidyddol eithafol ar y dde, ac, fel y gwelir yn achos y cerflun radio ym
Mae Caerdydd, mae ei rôl hanesyddol yn cael ei hailysgrifennu. Mae’n
rhesymol tybio bod ein teulu wedi cael ei ddal mewn ymgyrch wleidyddol
ehangach o’r chwith yn erbyn y dde, ac mai am roi llety i Marconi y bu i ni
wynebu canlyniadau canrif o hyd — problemau nad oedd yn bodoli yn y tair
canrif flaenorol yr oeddem wedi byw ar y fferm.

Roedd mam Marconi hefyd yn Jamerson o gwmni wisgi Gwyddelig Jameson. Rwy’n
gofyn i chi gynnal eich ymchwil eich hun, gwneud eich ymholiadau eich hun,
a dod i’ch casgliadau eich hun — ond yn anad dim, peidiwch â chaniatáu i
hanes gael ei ailysgrifennu yma.

Mae fy nheulu bellach yn archwilio opsiynau ar gyfer siarad cyhoeddus,
hawliau stori, a dogfennaeth. Yn nhermau cysylltiadau teuluol: fy nhaid
oedd Ray Smith o Dempsey and Makepeace; mae fy modryb yn Shan Cothi; a
dechreuodd fy ewythr y band Tigertailz.

Rwy’n disgrifio’r sefyllfa hon fel gwarthus. Mae fy nheulu’n mynnu
cyfiawnder am gael ein dadleoli a’n dwyn o’n tir a’n heiddo gan y Sefydliad
Prydeinig a BP, gyda phrin unrhyw amddiffyniad dan y gyfraith. Rydym yn
deulu Cymreig brodorol, Cymraeg eu hiaith, wedi byw yng Nghaerdydd, Bro
Morgannwg, a’r fferm yn Llandough ers cannoedd o flynyddoedd.

O’r hyn y gallaf ei gasglu, ceir dwsinau o achosion posibl o dwyll a
chuddio gwybodaeth, sy’n golygu nad yw statud cyfyngiadau yn berthnasol o
reidrwydd. I’r rhai sy’n cefnogi dad-drefedigaethu Cymru ac annibyniaeth,
prin y ceir enghraifft gliriach na *BP v Buckler (1987)* o’r hyn a
ddigwyddodd i deulu ffermio Cymreig wrth herio’r Wladwriaeth Brydeinig a
chorfforaeth fawr. Nid yw eraill wedi codi’r mater hwn, yn bennaf oherwydd
trawma cenhedlaethol.

Rwyf wedi profi fy hun. Gadewais fy ngyrfa filwrol gydag anrhydedd, gan
gwblhau fy llw 22 mlynedd. Cefais fy nghyflogi’n bona fide gan Gyngor Bro
Morgannwg a Llywodraeth Cymru hyd at 2024. Gwasanaethais mewn rhyfeloedd yn
y Dwyrain Canol. Fodd bynnag, nid yw’r anghyfiawnder fferm yn fater unigol.

Yn 2013, cafodd fy mab 36 diwrnod oed ei gipio, ac nid wyf erioed wedi ei
weld ers hynny. Cafodd tŷ ei ddwyn oddi arnaf (█████, Y Barri).
Yn 2023, cefais fy ngadael i gysgu mewn pabell tra roedd bron i 100 o
Afghanistaniaid yn cael eu lletya’n dawel wrth ymyl ein pentref o 11 tŷ,
tra roedd yn rhaid imi aros yno i ofalu am fy nain gan na allai gofalwyr ei
chyrraedd.

O ganlyniad, rwyf bellach yn byw yn yr hyn a elwir yn Setliad Cymreig yn yr
Ariannin. Rwyf wedi fy nisodli ac wedi fy dadleoli i’r eithaf. Serch hynny,
rwy’n ddiolchgar fy mod wedi goroesi gyda’m rhyddid, fy mywyd, a’m henw da
yn gymharol gyfan. Serch hynny, hoffwn fod wedi aros yng Nghymru, fel
Cymro, gyda safon a chynhaliaeth bywyd deg.

Mae fy ngwraig a minnau’n amharod i ganiatáu i’n merch hyd yn oed gamu ar
Ynysoedd Prydain o ystyried yr hyn a glywn sy’n digwydd yno. Yn 2024,
allforiais hyd yn oed fy nghi o Abertawe i’n heiddo yn y Caribî ar ôl i
unigolyn Afghanistan fod yng ngardd fy nheulu yng Nghymru, gan geisio ei
ddwyn.

Gofynnaf i’r Senedd gymryd y mater hwn o ddifrif, ac ystyried sefydlu
Ymchwiliad Cyhoeddus llawn, tryloyw ac annibynnol. Nid er budd fy nheulu yn
unig y mae hyn, ond er uniondeb hanes, cyfiawnder tir, a hawliau dynol yng
Nghymru.

Yn gywir,

*Requester*

*----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------*

Sirs/Ma'am,

I am writing to you regarding a significant historical injustice involving
my family, the Bucklers, and the destruction of Great House Farm (an
800-year-old site of monastic and Marconi history).

For example, in a 1974 press statement my grandmother said publically 'It's
my home'—that directly contradicts the 1987 Court of Appeal ruling that she
was 'silent' and accepted of BP license issued in 1974. My dad's appeal for
the BP vs Buckler 1987 case also got dismissed on grounds both BP Pension
Trust Ltd and BP Properties Ltd were effectively the same company. But in
the ruling he was appealing, the judge said that my nans replies to BP
Pensions Trust Ltd didn't count as BP Properties Ltd were the claimant, and
the two were seperate companies. So it was heads they win, tails we lose.
My dad was ripped from his hospital bed, jailed without charge and slapped
with a restraining order to keep him from occupying and defending our 800
year old farm from being bulldozed down. His ECHR request blocked before he
died in 1991 aged just 41.

I am requesting a *Petition for a Public Inquiry* into this case as a
matter of historical land theft and human rights violations in Wales.

I'm a military cyber and electronic warfare professional. We all have very
powerful AI technology at our disposal which can make light work out of all
of this. My family suffered an incredible injustice. It also appears to be
multi-generational warfare/ lawfare. Whereby we were treated as free labour
to upkeep the asset of the land and property until it was ripe to be cashed
in. I say this as every action against us seemed to be last minute.

There was allegedly press covering the 74 case and supporting my nan and
family and farm. There was a petition of 1700 people trying to defend us
and the farm from demolishment. CADW looked the other way when it should
have been a Grade II listed building. I could go on and on and on.

I'm not even sure the land registry recorded that our land, being
registered in 1982 by BP , was in dispute. I believe it was treated as if
it wasn't dispited. No court actually definitively determined that BP were
the landowners. It was just asserted.

Marconi stayed with our family at our farm when inventing radio. The
councillors and parish at Llandough won't even acknowledge this. I
understand Marconi was far right and so, like the radio statute at Cardiff
Bay has confirmed, he is being re-written out of history.  It stands to
reason that our family was caught in this political campaign of left vs
right. And for helping Marconi we found ourselves experiencing a century of
problems afterwards. Which didn't exist for the 3 centuries we were at our
farm before letting far right marconi stay with us. Marconi's mother was
also Jamerson of the Irish Whiskey company.

Do your own homework. Make your own enquiries. Draw your own conclusions.

 But please do not let history be rewritten here. My family are exploring
options for public speaking, story rights, and a documentary etc.

My grandfather was Ray Smith, of Dempsey and Makepeace. My aunty Shan
Cothi. My uncle started the band tigertailz.

This is an outrage and my family demands justice for being displaced and
█████ from, land and property, by the British Establishment/ BP -  with
little to no protections under law. And we're indigenous to the land,
Welsh, Welsh speaking, Welsh family. Resident in Cardiff / Vale and that
farm in Llandough for HUNDREDS OF YEARS.

There's tens of counts of █████ and concealment from what I can gather.
Which means the statute of limitation doesn't apply in this instance. I
know some are in favour of Wales decolonising and gaining independence. I
think there's no better example of BP vs Buckler 1987 and what has happened
to my family. Nobody else will bring this up because there's generational
trauma. Notwithstanding we, a welsh farming family, are speaking up and
against the British State and BP.

But I've proven myself. Leaving my military career with honours. Finishing
my 22 years Oath, bona fide, employed by the Vale of Glamorgan Council,
Welsh Government until 2024. I served in the wars in the middle east. I
don't know what is going on, on that island. But the farm injustice isn't
the only matter. My 36 day old son was abducted in 2013 and I've never seen
him since. I had a house █████ (█████, Barry). And in 2023 I
was left to sleep in a tent, while almost 100 afghans were secretly housed
next to our 11 home village. Where I had to be to care for my grandmother,
as no carers couldn't reach her. So I'm currently at the Welsh Settlement
in Argentina. So I'm as displaced and replaced as I can be to cater for the
insanity that's going on, on that island. And grateful I've managed to
survive it all with my liberty and life and reputation somewhat still
intact. But I would have actually liked to have remained in Wales as a
Welshman. And have some quality and standard of life. My wife and I are
reluctant for our daughter to even step foot on the British Isles with what
we're hearing that's going on there lately. And I even exported my dog from
Swansea to our place in the Caribbean in 2024 after an afghan was in my
family's garden in Wales, trying to steal him.

I look forward to your reply,

Regards,

Requester

Dear Committee Members,

I am writing to draw your attention to a historical land matter which I believe may illustrate potential vulnerabilities in public administration, record-keeping, and the governance of land registration. My purpose is solely to provide factual information for consideration, rather than to request remedial action.

The matter concerns land formerly known as Great House Farm, Llandough, Vale of Glamorgan, later developed for residential use and historically associated with BP v Buckler (Court of Appeal, 1987).

Chronology of relevant events (as reflected in public records):

  *   July 1974: Court proceedings involving my grandmother were adjourned without determination of ownership.
  *   31 October 1974: A subsequent hearing did not proceed substantively, following correspondence received from BP entities that same day. No judgment on ownership was issued.
  *   Throughout this period, my grandmother was not included in dealings concerning the land, while the opposing party continued to assert ownership.
  *   1982: The land was registered in the name of BP entities, despite unresolved competing █████ and no final judicial adjudication.
  *   1983: My grandmother passed away after the registration, with ownership never conclusively adjudicated.
  *   1987 Court of Appeal: The record reflects an apparent inconsistency in the treatment of correspondence and corporate entities. Specifically:

     *   The court noted that my grandmother had replied to correspondence on 31 October, asserting ownership.
     *   The reply was treated as directed to the “wrong” corporation (BP Pensions Trust Ltd rather than BP Properties Ltd).
     *   In a later appeal by my father, the same judge acknowledged that both BP entities were effectively treated as the same for the purposes of the ruling.
     *   These circumstances resulted in the court upholding the opposing party’s registration despite prior correspondence demonstrating an assertion of ownership.

  *   Following these proceedings, my father’s application to the European Court of Human Rights was blocked.
  *   The family home was demolished, preventing re-entry, even for the retrieval of personal belongings.
  *   Despite its historical significance and a petition to protect it, the property was not preserved. The house had prior heritage interest, including documented connections to Marconi.
  *   1991: My father passed away at just 41.
  *   1994: The land was subsequently excavated, with items of archaeological interest removed.

Taken together, these events demonstrate a situation in which land registration and subsequent reliance by public bodies proceeded without definitive adjudication of ownership, raising questions regarding administrative safeguards, procedural coherence, and record integrity.

I am submitting this information purely for institutional awareness. I am not making allegations of misconduct, nor requesting investigation. I am able to provide a concise factual timeline and references to public records should it assist the Committee’s understanding.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Is it not PACAC's role to ensure that the *machinery of the state*—the
courts, the Land Registry, and planning authorities—operates with
transparency and protects the constitutional rights of citizens against
administrative abuse? My case relates specifically to *maladministration*
and *constitutional overreach*: it involves the judicial "erasure" of a
320-year ancestral lineage through the tactical misnaming of Mary Williams
to "Mrs. Buckler", the administrative suppression of a known national
heritage site (the 1888 Roman find) to facilitate demolition permits, and
the suspicious disappearance of public title records from state-run
libraries. By focusing on how these public institutions failed to maintain
accurate records and fair procedures, I am  presenting a case of *systemic
failure in public administration*, which is the core reason I
understand your Committee to exist.

I must formally contest the assertion that this matter falls outside the
Committee’s remit. While the origin of this case involves a dispute with a
private entity (BP), the core of my grievance concerns *constitutional
issues* and the *quality of administration provided by government-funded
bodies*, specifically regarding the protection of national heritage and the
integrity of land registration.

I ask the Committee to review this matter under the following three pillars
of your mandate:

*1. Constitutional Issues: The Erasure of Customary and Indigenous Title* The
1987 Court of Appeal ruling (*BP Properties Ltd v Buckler*) created a
significant legal precedent regarding "unilateral licenses". My family
asserts that the administration of justice in this case allowed for the
tactical erasure of the "Williams" identity—a lineage with de facto
possession dating back to 1667—to facilitate a corporate land grab. The use
of the judicial system to overwrite centuries of documented continuity with
a "paper title" is a constitutional matter regarding the rights of citizens
against aggressive corporate-state interests.

*2. Standards of Administration: Suppression of Heritage by Public Bodies*
The Committee examines the quality of administration. My investigation
reveals that:

   -

   *Archaeological Suppression:* Evidence of a Roman soldier was discovered
   in 1888, providing "actual notice" of the site's significance. This was
   reportedly suppressed or ignored by planning authorities and the
   Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust (GGAT) to allow for demolition.

   -

   *Misrepresentation in Planning:* The 13th-century Great House Farm was
   administratively classified as a "dilapidated utility building" to bypass
   heritage protections.
   -

   *Missing Records:* Vital title evidence and Bute Estate deeds
   disappeared from the public library system—a failure of public record
   administration.


*3. Accountability of the Land Registry and Parliamentary Oversight* The
registration of this land under BP’s title occurred during a period of
transition in Welsh land law (c. 1982). If public registries accepted title
without disclosing active disputes or the presence of a known national
monument (the Roman/Medieval site), this represents a failure in the
"standards of administration" by the Civil Service. Furthermore, this
matter was raised in the House of Commons by MP Ted Rowlands in 1980, yet
the administrative failures continued unabated.

*Conclusion* I am not asking the Committee to act as a court of appeal, but
to investigate the *systemic administrative failures* that allowed a
historically significant site and a family's ancestral rights to be
"buried" through procedural maneuvers and the suppression of evidence.

If the Committee exists to ensure the Civil Service and constitutional
frameworks protect the public interest, then the demolition of an
800-year-old heritage site under a cloud of administrative "silence" must
be within your purview.


I look forward to your reconsidered response.


Sincerely,


Requester

surveys, and planning-era records may themselves be inaccurate or
incomplete as a result of earlier failures of disclosure. Specifically, a
Roman burial reportedly discovered at Great House Farm in 1888 appears to
have been treated as a “surprise” in later archaeological surveys

repeatedly described in planning documentation as an “old barn” or “utility
building.” These characterisations materially affected heritage protection,
culminating in demolition in 1988.

In that context, I am not seeking to pay for copies of records whose
accuracy is itself in question, nor to participate financially in processes
that may inadvertently perpetuate errors arising from that period. My
intention is to place relevant public bodies on notice of a potential issue
of public record integrity and heritage governance, not to obtain documents
for private interest. I have written to the Senedd calling for a public
enquiry too. I've notified the land registry and serious █████ teams too.

I am therefore asking that my correspondence be treated as a formal
expression of concern regarding the reliability and completeness of the
archival record as it relates to this site, and that this concern be noted
accordingly. I would also be grateful if you could advise which department
or officer is appropriate for addressing concerns of this nature, where the
issue is not access but potential historical misrepresentation within
public records.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am not alleging any impropriety on the part
of current archive staff. My concern relates to historical processes and
decisions, and to ensuring that those matters are properly examined rather
than inadvertently reinforced.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Yours sincerely,

Requester

Ms Smith,

Thanks for your reply and for explaining The National Archives’ position
regarding annotation and review of records.

I fully accept that archives do not resolve disputes and that records are
often incomplete or patchwork in character. My purpose in writing is not to
seek amendment, adjudication, or retrospective commentary, but to raise a
specific concern about how absence, silence, and fragmentation within the
archival record should be understood where material public consequences
clearly followed.

By way of clarification, my concern relates to the historical record
surrounding Great House Farm, Llandough, and the proceedings culminating in *BP
Properties Ltd v Buckler* [1987] EWCA Civ 2. In particular:

   - Ownership and occupation of the farmhouse and garden were actively
   contested in 1974, with a defence asserting adverse possession filed on
   behalf of Mary Williams, and the matter adjourned without a final
   determination of title.
   - Enforcement of earlier possession orders was deferred, a warrant was
   withdrawn on 31 October 1974, and the occupier remained in possession until
   her death in 1983.
   - Despite this, land registration, demolition (1988), and archaeological
   intervention proceeded without a High Court determination of ownership and
   without disclosure of earlier, locally known archaeological discoveries.
   - A Roman burial reportedly discovered beneath the farmhouse in 1888 by
   the occupying family appears not to have been reflected in later “rescue”
   excavations (1978–1980) or the major 1994 excavation, which treated Roman
   and early medieval burials as newly revealed.

Taken together, this produces an archival landscape in which:

   - court files relating to decisive events appear absent or incomplete;
   - later records imply finality where proceedings were in fact unresolved;
